title: The sheva brachos, and comforting mourners
summary: The brachos said under the chuppah, one at a time: why Hashem made ten chuppos for Adam and Chava, what "sameach tesamach" asks for, and why the last bracha can stand on its own. Then the Gemara turns to the brachos and words of comfort in a house of mourning, the ten cups of wine Chazal once drank there, and how Rabban Gamliel ended costly burials by asking to be buried in simple linen.
key_ideas: Each of the brachos under the chuppah has its own purpose, from yotzer ha'adam to the joy heard in the streets of Yerushalayim.
A double expression like sameach tesamach asks for joy that continues, not joy for one day.
The Baal Shem Tov's lesson from the sun and the moon: one who gives should never look at what the other is missing.
Chazal limited the wine drunk in a mourner's home, and Rabban Gamliel ended costly funerals by asking to be buried in simple linen.
